number.why: The source explicitly reports hospitalization for heart failure HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.61 to 0.88) for dapagliflozin versus placebo, with median follow-up of 4.2 years. The ruling correctly leaves the analysis set unstated: the held texts do not explicitly bind this estimate to intention-to-treat.

quotes.span: which reflected a lower rate of hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.88)
We randomly assigned patients with type 2 diabetes who had or were at risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease to receive either dapagliflozin or placebo.
We evaluated 17,160 patients, including 10,186 without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, who were followed for a median of 4.2 years.

entry.why: The sources establish adults with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease or risk. They do not establish actual inclusion of participants both with and without baseline heart failure. Absence of a heart-failure exclusion does not establish that composition, and absence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is not absence of heart failure.
